name: What can go wrong when replacing kitchen cabinets, especially in an older San Diego home?

mainEntity.name: What can go wrong when replacing kitchen cabinets, especially in an older San Diego home?

acceptedAnswer.text:
The biggest risks are ordering incorrect sizes, discovering moisture or wall damage after removal, overlooking appliance clearances, and assuming utility changes are included. A written scope and field verification reduce these problems.

**Context:** Cabinets may conceal plumbing leaks, uneven floors, or non-square walls. Moving a sink, adding circuits, changing gas service, or altering a wall can change both the work sequence and permit needs.

**Key factors:**
- Measure appliances before final cabinet approval
- Inspect for leaks and moisture damage
- Confirm filler panels, corner clearances, and door swings
- Identify utility changes before demolition

**Practical guidance:** Do not approve final cabinet orders until measurements and appliance specifications are checked. Keep a contingency for concealed conditions and ask how discovered issues will be documented.

Elite Remodeling & Design can review existing conditions during design and coordinate related construction work.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common problems include incorrect measurements, hidden leaks, uneven floors, out-of-square walls, appliance-clearance errors, and unplanned utility work. Verify appliances and wall conditions before ordering, and use a written process for documenting concealed conditions and changes.
